message.content:
{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study assesses the predictive capacity of AOT models using external validation with a dataset of 375 substances, comparing their predictions to known classifications. This quantifies the agreement between model predictions (animal model surrogate) and established classifications (human-relevant outcome).",
  "arm": "toxicology",
  "arm_evidence": "Several public efforts are aimed at discovering patterns or classifiers in the high-dimensional bioactivity space that predict tissue, organ or whole animal toxicological endpoints.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "cross-cutting"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study assesses Acute Oral Toxicity (AOT) and its relation to Globally Harmonized System (GHS) categories and Dangerous Goods (DG) classifications, which are broad safety assessments not tied to a specific therapeutic area.",
  "model_type": "in-vitro-or-in-silico-comparator",
  "model_evidence": "The study sought to assess and compare the predictions of the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) categories and Dangerous Goods (DG) classifications based on Lethal Dose (LD50) from several available tools (ACD/Labs, Leadscope, T.E.S.T., CATMoS, CaseUltra).",
  "species": [
    "not-species-specific"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study evaluates structure-activity relationship models for Acute Oral Toxicity (AOT) and Lethal Dose (LD50) predictions, which are general toxicological endpoints derived from animal studies but the models themselves are not species-specific.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study assesses predictions of GHS categories and DG classifications based on Lethal Dose (LD50), which are quantitative measures of toxicity but not primary hard clinical outcomes like mortality or survival."
}
